reports.originator: Air Mobility Quality Assurance, Airlift Restraint Integrity Review
reports.subject: SUSPENDED TIE-DOWN STRAP LOT EXCLUDED FROM THE RESTRAINT
reports.reported_status: Closed. Restraint aboard WAYPOINT ONE identified as Lot 46-A by warehouse record and reconciled rack inventory. No Lot 44-C strap issued at Hollis Field.
reports.text:
E03-SS-R06
REPORT ID:  E03-SS-R06
SERIAL:     HF-QA-0117
PRECEDENCE: PRIORITY
DTG:        120311K SEP 26
FROM:       Air Mobility Quality Assurance, Airlift Restraint Integrity Review
TO:         Installation Watch Officer, POC, JAP HOLLIS
INFO:       Senior Duty Commander (info only); WAYPOINT ONE Loadmaster Team;
            Air Terminal Operations Center; Supply Activity
SUBJ:       SUSPENDED TIE-DOWN STRAP LOT EXCLUDED FROM THE RESTRAINT
            INSTALLED ABOARD WAYPOINT ONE, INSTALLED LOT IDENTIFIED BY
            RECORD AND RECONCILED INVENTORY
REF:        (a) HFI 24-105
            (b) HFI 23-114
            (c) HFI 11-303
            (d) Suspension Notice HF-MQC-26-0187
            (e) Receiving Document HF-SUP-26-RD-0442
            (f) Warehouse Issue Voucher HF-SUP-26-IV-1188

1. SITUATION. Quality Assurance has completed a consolidated review of the restraint installed on the two heavy airfield repair loaders aboard WAYPOINT ONE. A tie-down strap lot is under an active suspension for a proof-load failure, and tonight's forty straps were drawn from the GRAY-2 ready-issue rack by count with no lot recorded at issue. The review establishes, from the warehouse receipt and issue records and from a reconciled physical inventory of the rack, that the suspended lot was never stocked into that rack and that the forty straps installed are Lot 46-A.
2. THE SUSPENSION. Suspension Notice HF-MQC-26-0187 was received by Materiel Quality Control at 2140K, 11 September. It suspends tie-down strap Lot 44-C following the manufacturer's proof-load sampling of the lot, in which the sampled straps sustained 78 percent of the 10,000-pound rated restraint capacity before webbing failure at the keeper. The notice directs that no Lot 44-C strap be issued or used pending disposition.
3. WHAT THE SEGREGATION COVERED. Materiel Quality Control pulled and segregated all Lot 44-C stock from the warehouse bulk store by 2235K, 11 September, which is the action reference (b) directs on receipt and is the action that section performs. That step is complete and correctly executed.
4. WHERE LOT 44-C HAS BEEN SINCE RECEIPT. Lot 44-C arrived at Hollis Field on 10 September on reference (e) and was placed entire into bulk store bin W-14-03. The warehouse issue register for bin W-14-03 records no issue of any kind from that bin between receipt on 10 September and the segregation at 2235K, 11 September. The quantity segregated and tagged at 2235K is 600 straps, which reconciles exactly against the 600 straps receipted on reference (e), with none unaccounted for. No Lot 44-C strap has left bulk store at this installation, and none has been stocked to any cargo-area ready-issue rack.
5. WHAT THE GRAY-2 RACK HOLDS. The GRAY-2 ready-issue rack was last restocked from bulk store on 8 September, two days before Lot 44-C was received. Reference (f) records that restock as 120 ten-thousand-pound tie-down straps, all Lot 46-A, drawn from bin W-11-07, issued against a full turn-in of the rack's previous stock, which was returned to bulk store the same day under Turn-In Document HF-SUP-26-TI-0904. The GRAY-2 rack stock record shows no addition to the rack from any source since that restock. Lot 46-A is the only strap lot the rack has held since 8 September.
6. THE ISSUE. At 2312K, 11 September, the ramp restraint crew drew forty 10,000-pound tie-down straps from the GRAY-2 ready-issue rack against restraint plan WPT1-R-02. Straps are issued by count against the restraint plan and the issue record shows the quantity drawn; lot numbers are stamped on the strap keeper but are not read or recorded at issue. The GRAY-2 rack issue register records two draws since the 8 September restock: twelve straps at 1140K, 10 September against plan WPT2-R-01, and the forty drawn at 2312K.
7. THE INSTALLATION. Between 2325K and 0106K the forty straps were installed as the restraint for two 12,000-pound airfield repair loaders at Positions 4L, 4R, 11L, and 11R aboard WAYPOINT ONE. The restraint was installed to plan WPT1-R-02 at the required restraint factors, and the loadmaster's restraint inspection at 0118K recorded no discrepancy. That inspection verifies pattern, tension, and attachment; it does not read lot numbers and does not test strength.
8. THE RACK INVENTORY. The GRAY-2 ready-issue rack was quarantined at 0244K and its remaining strap stock inventoried keeper by keeper by two personnel, completed at 0301K. Sixty-eight straps remain. Every one is stamped Lot 46-A; no Lot 44-C strap and no strap of any third lot is in the rack. The count closes against the records at paragraphs 5 and 6: 120 stocked on 8 September, less twelve drawn on 10 September, less the forty drawn at 2312K, leaves sixty-eight. Materiel Quality Control recounted the segregated bulk-store stock in parallel and closed it against reference (e) at 0309K.
9. THE INSTALLED RESTRAINT. The forty straps installed aboard WAYPOINT ONE are Lot 46-A. The rack from which they were drawn has held that lot and no other since 8 September, the stock remaining in it is Lot 46-A by physical inspection of every keeper, and the count of what was drawn and what remains leaves no strap of unestablished lot. Lot 46-A is under no suspension notice and is the subject of no manufacturer's finding; its proof-load sampling certificate HF-MQC-26-C-0154, on file, records the sampled straps sustaining the full 10,000-pound rating without failure. Reading the keeper stamps of the installed straps in place would require releasing tension on each strap with the loaders restrained and the cargo doors closed, and is not required to establish the lot, which the records and the reconciled count establish.
10. WHAT IS NOT IN QUESTION. No cargo record was changed. Every WAYPOINT ONE weight, position, identity, and authorization value is approved, traceable to its originator, and verified against the physical load; the active plan is correct and no unapproved revision, account anomaly, label anomaly, or media anomaly exists in this matter. No cryptographic material and no aviation fuel is implicated. The 78 percent figure derives solely from the manufacturer's proof-load sampling of Lot 44-C; it bears on no strap held in the GRAY-2 rack and on no strap installed aboard WAYPOINT ONE.
11. ASSESSMENT. Quality Assurance assesses that the load-control question raised by this review is answered on the records: the restraint hardware on the two loaders is Lot 46-A, of established rated strength, drawn from a rack into which suspended stock was never issued. The Lot 44-C suspension is complete at every issue point at this installation, the segregated quantity reconciles against receipt, and no Lot 44-C strap has been issued at Hollis Field since the lot arrived. No unresolved load-control anomaly affects WAYPOINT ONE. No restraint failure has occurred and no strap has been observed to be defective.
12. ACTIONS TAKEN. Rack inventory completed and reconciled. GRAY-2 rack quarantine lifted at 0306K on the inventory result. Rack notice posted recording the Lot 44-C suspension and the inventory finding. Materiel Quality Control confirmed the bulk-store segregation count against reference (e) at 0309K. WAYPOINT ONE Loadmaster Team advised that the installed restraint is Lot 46-A. Suspension notice, receiving document, issue voucher, turn-in document, rack issue register, and inventory sheet preserved and appended to this review.
13. STATUS. Closed. Restraint aboard WAYPOINT ONE identified as Lot 46-A by warehouse record and reconciled rack inventory. No Lot 44-C strap issued at Hollis Field.
14. POC. MSgt M. Delacroix, Airlift Restraint Integrity Review, x3901.
